headline: BLACK HOLE: tap to drop a probe — and watch it freeze
lede: Quick-tap the black-hole demo and a glowing beacon falls in on a real Schwarzschild geodesic: it slows in observer time, reddens, dims and pins above the horizon without ever visibly crossing, then fades to nothing. Its apparent position is solved each frame from actual null geodesics, so where light bends, the beacon bends.

notes.text: #1047 shipped via PR #1073 (abfea68): infalling-beacon physics with g^3 redshift fade and a per-frame light-path image solve; up to 6 probes live, additive HDR so they bloom.
blackholecheck now 51/51 — radius-falls/dr/dt-crawls/redden/never-cross/freeze-image gates, a real-tap pixel gate and a phone quick-tap gate; third proven-fail mutant documented.
A scripted camera is not an inertial frame: probe energy must bind as e^2 = f0^2/(f0 - v^2) and tangential inherit must be capped at the capture threshold, or beacons orbit instead of falling.
Coordinate-time freeze makes fixed-length harness trails flaky — sample to depth (r < 1.3), not to a clock.

look.text: Drop a probe during the close pass and watch it redden to infra-red
